content.intro: This lesson covers Fn, FnMut, and FnOnce. It sits in Module 13, Closures and Iterator-Based Programming, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Fn, FnMut, and FnOnce matters when you work with type-safe program design. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A closure can capture values from its surrounding environment. Its Fn, FnMut, or FnOnce behavior depends on whether it only borrows captured values, mutates them, or consumes them.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Fn, FnMut, and FnOnce, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Closures capture variables according to how the body uses them. Most iterator adaptors are lazy until a terminal consumer runs.
